note: One source of truth for place names, read by scripts/build_site.py (which refuses to ship a city under a local name) and scripts/passcheck.py (which needs to translate in both directions). Keys are the local spelling, values are the English name this site publishes under. Direction matters and has bitten twice: matching a published city needs local-to-English, while finding candidates in a register needs English-to-local, because registers file Genoa as Genova and Padua as Padova.
why_english: Every page on this site is written in English and its readers search in English, so the site publishes Florence rather than Firenze and Naples rather than Napoli. This is not a translation policy for prose: an entry's address, its register name and any quoted source keep the local spelling, because that is what a visitor reads on the street sign and what the paperwork actually says.
only_real_differences: Every pair here must be a genuine difference between the local name and current English usage. Never add an identity pair (krakow -> krakow): the build check reads a key as proof the name is wrong, so an identity pair would fail the build on a correct city. Never add an archaic exonym either. English has dropped Leghorn for Livorno and Saragossa for Zaragoza, and reviving one would be the same mistake pointing the other way.
no_exonym_exists: Most places have no separate English name and must not be given one: Bologna, Porto, Trieste, Lucca, Verona, Caserta, Palermo, Setubal, Guimaraes, Bucaco, Cordoba, Granada, Malaga, Valencia, Zaragoza, Krakow, Gdansk, Kyoto, Osaka, Helsinki, Ljubljana. Leaving these alone is correct.
